parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the features of the self report method and outline how it was used in the Loftus and
Pickrell study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative study of false memories using the case study method and describe
how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Evaluate this alternative way of studying false memories in methodological and ethical terms.

text: Loftus and Pickrell used self reports to investigate false memories. An alternative way to
investigate false memories would be to conduct a case study.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by ‘ethical guidelines’ in psychology?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one ethical guideline that was broken in the Bandura et al. study.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of attempting to meet ethical guidelines, using
the Bandura et al. study as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss the extent to which the Bandura et al. study is reliable. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Bandura et al. investigated aggression using children, this has advantages and disadvantages.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘longitudinal method’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Freud (little Hans)
Haney, Banks and Zimbardo (prison simulation)
Thigpen and Cleckley (multiple personality disorder)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the behaviours investigated in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: What problems may psychologists have when they use the longitudinal method?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘cognitive approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Held and Hein (kitten carousel)
Mann et al. (lying)
Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the cognitive processes that were investigated in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they investigate cognitive processes?
